ns2:section.sectionText: InterStellar Medium: 4 credit hours In this course, students will learn practical knowledge of the interstellar medium (ISM) and skills to carry out observational research and write papers and grant proposals. Lectures will be given on selected topics of the ISM. Students are required to use archival X-ray (Chandra, XMM, and ROSAT), UV (IUE, FUSE, HST STIS/COS), optical (HST), IR (Spitzer, Herschel, HST), gamma-ray (Fermi) data to study specific problems, present the results in a publishable paper, and/or write a proposal requesting funding for the research. There will be homeworks, a mid-term oral presentation of their research progess, and a final paper reporting the research results. x 496
